Phase 2 (highest-risk, STOP-gated) is BLOCKED: openBranch_countermodel/tableau_complete's byte-stable (Postmortem 5) signatures pin IForces's World argument to bare Nat, forcing Lean to resolve [Preorder Nat] to the unique global Nat.instPreorder (verified live via #synth Preorder Nat) -- a TOTAL, unbounded order. blockers.title: Edge-accessibility frame cannot be installed without changing openBranch_countermodel/tableau_complete's byte-stable signatures, or IForces's definition
blockers.detail: IForces (Kripke.lean:81) is generic over [Preorder World]; its .imp case resolves '<=' via typeclass search on World. openBranch_countermodel and tableau_complete (Scheme.lean:1320-1336, 1360-1368) both state IForces (intExtractValuation b) (S.modelBot b) 0 phi with intExtractValuation b : Nat -> Atom -> Prop (Soundness.lean:1811, unchanged type) and 0 : Nat, so World unifies to Nat and Lean resolves [Preorder Nat] to the unique global Nat.instPreorder -- confirmed live via '#synth Preorder Nat' (returns Nat.instPreorder) and 'example : (Preorder.toLE : LE Nat).le = (. <= .) := rfl' (typechecks). This resolution happens at theorem-type elaboration time, before any proof-body tactic (letI/haveI) could override it, so no completeness-side-only edit can install edge-accessibility for these two theorems without changing their stated types.
blockers.counterexample: Report 08's adversarial example, re-verified: branch carries T((not p) -> q)@0 on an open saturated branch. Pick phantom world k strictly larger than every branch label. intExtractValuation b j p = False for every phantom j (nothing labeled j on the branch), so IForces k (not p) = (forall j>=k, IForces j p -> IForces j bot) is vacuously True (antecedent always False). But IForces k q = intExtractValuation b k q = False (phantom). So k witnesses IForces k (not p) and not(IForces k q), refuting 'forall w'>=0, w' forces (not p) -> w' forces q' -- i.e. the T(->) truth-lemma case (sorry 330) is genuinely FALSE at World=Nat/canonical order, for ANY branch containing this shape of T-implication.
blockers.new_finding_beyond_report_08: Nat.instPreorder is a LINEAR (total) order; general intuitionistic Kripke-completeness requires NON-LINEAR (tree/DAG-shaped) frames in general (e.g. two beta-split sibling worlds are edge-incomparable, yet both receive SOME Nat label under a total order). No relabelling/retraction of edge-accessible worlds onto bare Nat can make a total order represent a genuinely non-linear accessibility relation. This rules out any 'clever reindexing' workaround within the existing World=Nat commitment, not just the current numeric-labelling scheme -- the obstruction is type-theoretic, not merely a missing proof.
blockers.recommendation: Requires a human/orchestrator-level architectural decision before Phase 2 can proceed. Two escape routes, both outside 'completeness-side edits + read-only soundness machinery': (a) change openBranch_countermodel's/tableau_complete's stated conclusion types to quantify over a new World type carrying a custom edge-based Preorder instance -- a deliberate, tracked public-signature change, requiring Postmortem Constraint 5 to be revised in a plan v6, plus an audit of all Decidable/DecisionProcedure consumers; (b) change IForces's definition (Kripke.lean) to take an explicit accessibility relation parameter instead of relying on [Preorder World] -- a foundational semantics change rippling into the already-green tableau_sound (same file, task-316-adjacent) and other IForces consumers, forbidden without escalation per Postmortem 4.
